messages.content: Thanksgiving update: my sister can handle meals in San Diego but not four overnight guests, and the drive is officially out. The Southwest quote from the family text moved, so can you help me lock the real flight and hotel before I buy? Four of us, SLC to San Diego Wednesday 11/27 and back Sunday 12/1.

Yes. Since the choice affects both Monday recovery and baggage cost, I want to check two things first: do you want to protect Monday morning over getting extra Sunday family time, and are you planning checked bags or mostly carry-ons?
Protect Monday. One checked family bag at most, plus carry-ons. I would also rather not rent a car unless it makes the weekend dramatically easier.

Here is the practical shortlist. Flight option A: Delta nonstop, SLC 4:55 PM to SAN 5:55 PM Wednesday; return SAN 4:40 PM to SLC 7:35 PM Sunday. About $1,684 for four, plus about $70 total if you check one bag both ways, assigned seats available. Flight option B: Southwest nonstop around 5:20 PM Wednesday and later Sunday; now about $1,790, bags included, open seating. Hotel option A: Hampton Inn San Diego-Kearny Mesa, two queens, refundable, breakfast and self-parking included, about $756 before tax. Option B: the closer holiday hotel is a little nearer your relatives but has tighter cancellation, weaker dinner access, and parking is not as clean. I would take Delta with the 4:40 Sunday return, Hampton, and no rental car.
I can live with Delta if we can choose seats. Can we get at least one window for the kids? And is 4:40 too early if Sunday lunch runs long?

Right now Delta Main Cabin has 16A/16B and 17A/17B open, so that gives you two pairs and two windows. The Sunday flight means leaving the family gathering around 2:00 PM, maybe 1:45 if you are farther north. The evening return buys more visiting time but gets everyone home close to bedtime and leaves less room for holiday delays.
That makes sense. Before I book, can you verify the Hampton breakfast and parking are actually included? I do not want a holiday surprise.

The Hampton listing shows complimentary breakfast daily and complimentary self-parking. For Thanksgiving week I would still add a note to confirm holiday breakfast hours, but it is not showing as a paid add-on. The two-queen nonsmoking room is refundable until Monday 11/25 at 11:59 PM hotel time.
Okay, reserve that hotel. For the flights, book Delta with the 4:40 Sunday return, one checked bag, and those paired seats if still open.
I can do that. Last local-transport check: are your relatives definitely handling Wednesday airport pickup and the Thanksgiving/Friday shuttling, with you using rideshare back to SAN on Sunday?
Yes. My sister will grab us Wednesday, cousins can move us around for the main meals, and we will rideshare to the airport Sunday. No rental.
Great. I will book the Delta flights, reserve the Hampton, and leave out the rental. Use the family traveler info already on file?
Yes, use the family traveler info. Send me the version I can paste into the group text with the cancellation date and baggage plan.

Booked summary for the family thread: We are flying Delta Main Cabin nonstop SLC to San Diego on Wednesday 11/27, 4:55 PM to 5:55 PM, and returning Sunday 12/1, 4:40 PM to 7:35 PM. Seats requested in pairs: 16A/16B and 17A/17B, subject to aircraft changes. We will check one shared bag, about $35 each way, and carry on the rest. Hotel is Hampton Inn San Diego-Kearny Mesa, two queens, breakfast included, free self-parking, refundable until Monday 11/25 at 11:59 PM, about $756 before tax. No rental car: family pickup Wednesday, relatives for local rides, rideshare to SAN Sunday.

messages.content: Quick San Diego pretrip check. The hotel emailed asking whether to add a late-arrival note for Wednesday, and the Delta app moved our seats after an aircraft swap. We still have one window pair, but the other two are split farther back. Friday lunch also moved earlier.

Yes to the late-arrival note. For the 4:55 PM SLC flight with four people and one checked bag, aim to be at the airport by 2:45 PM and leave home around 2:05. On seats, do you want me to prioritize keeping people in pairs, or chase window seats even if that splits you up?
Pairs first. One window is nice, but I do not want kids separated from an adult.
Then keep 16A/16B for one pair. I can move the other pair from 18C/18D to 17C/17D, which keeps them closer. No adjacent window pair is open now, but it is worth checking again at the 24-hour mark.
Do that. And can you add the hotel note and verify two queens, breakfast hours, and parking?

Done. The hotel has a late-arrival note for Wednesday evening, with the card on file holding the room. They confirmed a nonsmoking two-queen room, complimentary self-parking, and breakfast currently listed 6:00 to 10:00 AM over the holiday weekend. They cautioned holiday staffing can shift the setup slightly, but coffee should be available earlier.
Friday lunch moved to 11:30 near La Jolla. Does that mess with anything?
No. It just makes Friday morning tighter. Breakfast at the hotel around 8:30 or 9:00, then plan to leave Kearny Mesa by about 10:45 depending on traffic and who is driving you.
And what is our Sunday leave-by time for the 4:40 return?

Leave the family gathering by 2:00 PM, or 1:45 if you are north of La Jolla or still need to check the bag. That should put you at SAN around 2:30 for a busy holiday Sunday. Final checklist: leave home Wednesday around 2:05, check one shared bag, seats are paired at 16A/16B and 17C/17D, Hampton late-arrival note is added, two queens/breakfast/free parking are confirmed, and use rideshare to the airport Sunday.

messages.content: Now that Thanksgiving is behind us, I have a January Denver workshop to figure out. It is downtown, starts Monday Jan. 13 at 1:00 PM, runs all day Tuesday, and closes Wednesday at 11:30. Can you compare a Sunday afternoon flight, a Monday morning flight, and driving from Salt Lake? I also need the official hotel block compared with nearby hotels that include breakfast.
Absolutely. Before I rank them, is there any required prep before the 1:00 PM Monday kickoff, and would the extra Sunday hotel night be reimbursable if it is justified for winter arrival reliability?

No prep before 1:00, but I cannot be late. The university will reimburse either airfare or mileage. An extra night should be okay if the reason is solid. I do not need a car downtown, and breakfast matters Tuesday because the agenda starts at 8:00.

Then my ranking is: Sunday afternoon nonstop flight first, Monday morning flight a distant second, and driving only if the forecast is unusually clear. Sunday flying gives you a buffer, avoids I-80/I-25 winter risk, and lets you arrive before dinner. Monday morning technically works, but one cancellation or deicing delay could put the 1:00 kickoff at risk. Driving is reimbursable, but it adds fatigue, road-closure uncertainty, and downtown parking.
Can you put numbers around it? My director will ask why I am not just driving.

Driving is roughly 520 miles each way, so the reimbursed mileage can be substantial before you even add downtown parking at about $40 to $55 per night. It is also 8 to 9.5 hours each way in good weather. A nonstop flight is likely in the $220 to $320 range, plus airport train or rideshare. The Sunday hotel night is the extra cost, but it directly protects an on-time Monday arrival.
What if I flew Monday morning on the first nonstop?

The first nonstop can work on paper: leave SLC around 7:00 AM, land around 8:30, and get downtown by 10:00 if everything runs cleanly. The problem is that January deicing or a cancellation leaves very little recovery room. A 9:00 AM departure is too tight for a mandatory 1:00 PM start. If you must do Monday, use the first nonstop, carry on only, and keep the organizer warned. I would not choose it if Sunday is reimbursable.
Okay, Sunday afternoon flight. I do not need a rental car. What hotel options look reasonable?

For Sunday Jan. 12 to Wednesday Jan. 15, I would compare these: official workshop hotel block at $229 per night, about a 2-minute covered walk to the meeting space, no breakfast included, on-site restaurant, and parking around $49 if you drove. Hampton downtown/Convention Center area at about $174, breakfast included, queen room, 6- to 8-minute walk or short rideshare, casual food nearby. Home2 or Hyatt Place downtown at about $181 to $189, breakfast included, larger room, closer to 10 minutes on foot, with dinner nearby but less convenient in cold weather.
Breakfast is appealing, but a 10-minute icy walk after a reception is not. Is the Hampton walk exposed?

Mostly exposed, though it is straightforward. If sidewalks are icy, budget short rideshares for morning or evening moves, maybe $8 to $15 each. The official block wins on convenience and late-night food. Hampton wins on breakfast and rate. Since you are flying, the official hotel parking fee should not matter unless plans change and you drive.
Does the official block's lack of breakfast create a receipt problem?

Not a problem, just more line items. With the official hotel, breakfast would come out of per diem or a separate meal receipt. With Hampton, breakfast is included on the room folio, which simplifies early Tuesday. For the official hotel, watch for destination fees or dining credits because Concur may need those explained.
Can we hold two refundable rooms while I ask my director? One official block and one breakfast option.

Yes, as long as neither is prepaid. I would hold the official block as the weather-and-convenience backup and Hampton as the cost-conscious primary. Same dates: Sunday Jan. 12 check-in, Wednesday Jan. 15 checkout. It is just you for this trip, correct, and a standard queen room is fine?
Just me. Queen is fine, non-smoking, and no prepaid rates. I also want dinner access Sunday after landing.

That points to two sensible holds. Hampton is fine if you arrive early evening: there are casual restaurants nearby, and Union Station or the theater district is a short rideshare. The official block is easier if you land late or it is snowing because the restaurant is in the building. I will add late Sunday arrival possible, non-smoking, quiet room if available.
For flights, what is the best Sunday afternoon target from SLC, and what should I do Wednesday after the 11:30 close?

For Sunday, target a nonstop leaving SLC between about 2:30 and 5:00 PM. That gets you downtown by dinner without burning the whole day. For Wednesday, book DEN to SLC no earlier than 2:30 PM; that gives you time to leave the venue around noon, get to the airport by train or rideshare, and still have a comfortable security buffer.
Great. Hold the two hotels and send me the argument for Sunday flight over driving.

Held: official workshop hotel block, standard queen, non-smoking, Sunday Jan. 12 to Wednesday Jan. 15, cancelable until Jan. 9 at 6:00 PM; and Hampton downtown/Convention Center area, queen room, breakfast included, non-smoking, same dates, cancelable until Jan. 10 at 4:00 PM. Director note: Sunday afternoon nonstop is recommended because the workshop has a mandatory Monday 1:00 PM start, January driving across Wyoming and northern Colorado has meaningful closure and delay risk, and driving would add mileage reimbursement plus downtown parking. Flying with airport train or rideshare avoids a rental car, reduces fatigue, and creates a defensible arrival buffer. Next step is to release one hotel once your director confirms the lodging approach.
